chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: A man rises when it has already become light at the time of the morning prayer? He said: Then let him perform the two rak'ahs that are before al-ghadah, then let him perform al-ghadah.

And the other possibility is that it is to be understood as carried upon a kind of taqiyyah, because that is the doctrine of most of the 'ammah, and none agrees with us on it except a small number. And that which indicates this is...

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under particular circumstances
key_terms.السَّجْدَتَيْنِ: the two rak'ahs meant before the morning prayer
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the Sunni majority or the general non-Shi'i community in this context
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the morning prayer time, referring here to fajr
key_terms.نُوِّرَ: the appearance of light or brightness at dawn

ai.seo_question: If dawn has already brightened, should one still perform the two rak'ahs before the morning prayer?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on the two rak'ahs before the morning prayer when a person rises after the sky has already brightened. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that the two rak'ahs be performed first and then the morning prayer, while the closing note indicates another interpretive possibility related to taqiyyah in light of the view held by most of the 'ammah.
